newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures scuppered by U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures scuppered by U.S. jobs data.

text.p: A mid-afternoon report showing stronger-than-expected jobs growth in the U.S. in December sent German Bunds into negative territory in late dealings, dashing earlier hopes for an end-of-week rally.
March Bund futures were down 21 basis points at 100.10, off a session high of 100.46, after a session with what dealers said were the highest volumes since December 10.
But dealers described the market reaction as a moderate response to U.S. debt markets' tumble on a report showing U.S. jobs rose by 262,000 in December, far above forecasts for a rise of 192,000.
The outlook for Bunds was uncertain, dealers said, with the market constantly falling victim to U.S. market developments, despite a far more positive environment on the home front.

Bunds' earlier gains had been supported by the theory that the present cold spell gripping Germany and Europe will dampen most economic growth for the current period and by expectations for prolonged low interest rates in Germany.
"The market is trapped between its traditional high level of correlation with U.S debt and the fact that economic prospects for the two countries are completely different," said one Frankfurt dealer.
